## Why visit

A beer-focused café with enough cask depth to justify a stop even on a traditional-ale trip. Its bottle selection provides an opportunity to explore wild fermentation and sharing bottles without leaving the centre, and the cheese or meat plates offer a useful pause between pubs. It works particularly well with City Arms and the chop houses: the surroundings change completely, but beer remains the point. Make time to inspect the fridges and ask for a recommendation beyond whatever is easiest to recognise.

## Beer

CAMRA reports seven cask lines including a Runaway house beer and changing British guests, plus keg and an extensive international bottle selection. CAMRA specifically identifies Runaway Stone’s Throw as its regular house cask; the rest of the seven-line cask selection rotates.

## Food

Cheese and meat plates and other bar snacks are documented; useful for a light food stop.

## Plan the visit

The public entrance is on Brown Street, despite some addresses saying Spring Gardens. Card only; check corkage/drink-in supplements before choosing large bottles. Central Manchester CAMRA Pub of the Year 2026.

**Getting there:** Walk from Market Street tram stop; convenient for City Arms and the Cross Street chop houses.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
